statement.p: Suppose that the density of cars (in cars per mile) down a 20-mile stretch of the Pennsylvania Turnpike is approximated by \delta(x) = 300 \left(2+\sin\left(4\sqrt{x + 0.175}\right)\right), at a distance x miles from the Breezewood toll plaza. Sketch a graph of this function for 0\leq x\leq 20.
(a) Complete the Riemann sum that approximates the total number of cars on this 20-mile stretch (use Dx instead of \Delta x):
(b) Find the total number of cars on the 20-mile stretch.

static.solution:
(a) Suppose we choose an x, 0\le x\le 20. We approximate the density of the number of the cars between x and x+\Delta x miles as \delta(x) cars per mile. Therefore, the number of cars between x and x+\Delta x is approximately \delta(x)\Delta x. If we slice the 20 mile strip into N slices, we get that the total number of cars is C \approx \Sigma_{i=1}^N \delta(x_i)\Delta x = \Sigma_{i=1}^N \left[ 600 + 300\sin(4\sqrt{x_i + 0.175})\right]\Delta x, where \Delta x =20/N. This is a right-hand approximation; the corresponding left-hand approximation is \Sigma_{i=0}^{N-1}\delta(x_i)\Delta x. We can more loosely write both approximations without referring to the number of steps as C \approx \Sigma \left[ 600 + 300\sin(4\sqrt{x + 0.175})\right]\Delta x.
(b) As N\to\infty, the Riemann sum above approaches the integral C =\int_0^{20} (600 + 300\sin4\sqrt{x + 0.175})\,dx. If we calculate the integral numerically, we find C\approx 11499.5. We can also find the integral exactly as follows: C = \int_0^{20} (600 + 300\sin4\sqrt{x +0.175})\,dx = \int_0^{20} 600\,dx +\int_0^{20} 300\sin4\sqrt{x + 0.175}\,dx = 12000 + 300\int_0^{20}\sin4\sqrt{x +0.175}\,dx. Let w = \sqrt{x +0.175}, so x =w^2 -0.175 and dx =2w\,dw. Then \int_{x=0}^{x=20}\sin 4\sqrt{x +0.175}\,dx = 2\int_{w=\sqrt{0.175}}^{w=\sqrt{20.175}} w\sin 4w\,dw, = 2\left[-{1\over 4}w\cos 4w +{1\over 16}\sin 4w\right] \bigg|_{\sqrt{0.175}}^{\sqrt{20.175}} \approx -1.55. (To find the integral we used the appropriate entry in a table of integrals.) Using this, we have C\approx 12000 + 300(-1.55) \approx 11499.5, which matches our numerical approximation.
